claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g cm^-3.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a yield strength of approximately 855 MPa near 1000 °C.
Replacing approximately 25% of the Hf content with Y will lower the alloy density.
Replacing approximately 25% of the Hf content with Y will preserve solid-solution strengthening.
Replacing approximately 25% of the Hf content with Y will preserve phase stability.
The Y-substituted alloy will retain a stable single-phase microstructure.
Solid-solution strengthening and phase stability confer the alloy's room- and high-temperature yield strengths.
Y has significantly lower atomic mass and density than Hf.
Y has refractory character and high-temperature stability comparable to Hf in the proposed alloy.
The atomic size of Y is sufficiently similar to that of Hf to maintain strengthening lattice distortion.
Y substitution will maintain dislocation-hardening effects at room temperature and 1000 °C.
The Y-substituted alloy will have a density at least 5% below the 10.21 g cm^-3 baseline.
The room-temperature yield strength of the Y-substituted alloy will remain within ±10% of 1600 MPa.
The 1000 °C yield strength of the Y-substituted alloy will remain within ±10% of 855 MPa.

contradictions.description: The baseline is explicitly described as as-cast, but the experiment says samples will be cast and heat-treated under conditions identical to that as-cast baseline. A post-casting heat treatment cannot be identical to an as-cast condition unless the stated heat treatment is omitted or separately defined.
